name: Poland
summary_text: Poland is broadly workable with two genuinely traveler-relevant weaknesses and a low-but-improving social baseline. In detention, Poland has documented severe failures involving foreign trans people directly: a Vietnamese trans woman was held in a male immigration-detention center with her hormone-therapy needs ignored, and the European Court of Human Rights found Poland violated a trans prisoner's rights by denying her HRT (2024). There is no specialized trans prison section analogous to Italy's Rebibbia. Socially, the climate was deeply hostile under the previous Law and Justice government ("LGBT-free zones") and is improving under the Tusk coalition (a hate-speech reform draft in March 2025; ceased investigating foreign same-sex marriages), but a low baseline persists — Pride marches have been violently attacked (Białystok 2019), online anti-LGBT harassment is documented (Amnesty 2025), and rural areas draw harassment warnings. Legal gender recognition is court-based and medically gatekept, with no self-ID. Bathrooms are unrestricted and there is no cross-dressing statute. Major cities are calmer than rural areas.

sources.title: Transgender woman released from a guarded center for male foreigners - Association for Legal Intervention
sources.claim_summary: Association for Legal Intervention (SIP) news (March 2024): a transgender Vietnamese citizen was placed by a Polish regional court in a guarded centre for male foreigners despite identifying as a woman and undergoing hormone therapy since 2018 (stopping would be detrimental); SIP secured her release - documenting detention-placement problems for trans migrants in Poland.

sources.title: ECtHR rules Polish prison authorities violated trans woman's rights by denying access to hormone therapy - TGEU - Trans Europe and Central AsiaTGEU – Trans Europe and Central Asia
sources.claim_summary: TGEU (July 2024): the ECtHR ruled Polish prison authorities violated a trans woman's Article 8 rights by denying her access to hormone replacement therapy in prison (EUR 8,000 damages) - strengthening trans prisoners' right to life-saving treatment.

ECHR Case Law summary of W.W. v. Poland (11 July 2024, app. 31842/20): a trans prisoner diagnosed with gender dysphoria was denied continuation of hormone therapy after transfer; the burden imposed on her to prove the necessity of treatment was disproportionate - violation of private life.

Amnesty International report (Sept 2025) 'A Thousand Cuts': technology-facilitated gender-based violence against Poland's LGBTI community on X - quantitative experiment and content labelling documenting targeted online abuse.

sources.title: World Report 2025: Poland | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: HRW World Report 2025 Poland chapter: the Tusk coalition government began addressing rule-of-law concerns from the PiS era; includes a Sexual Orientation and Gender Identity section.

ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2025 (covering 2024) chapter on Poland: new hate-speech law plans (January) expanding protections to gender identity and sexual orientation; a second bill (October) notably omitted gender identity as a protected category; a mayor was sentenced for a homophobic letter to the PM; legislative flux on hate-crime protections.
Government of Canada travel advice for Poland (updated Aug 2026): 'Take normal security precautions'. General travel advice, not trans-specific.

Polish legal journal article (Przegląd Sejmowy, 2024, in Polish) by Podgórska-Rykała and Kępa: 'Current Legal and Administrative Situation of Transgender Persons in Poland. Selected Issues' - analyses the Civil Status Records Law, Population Register Act and Identity Cards Act and their impact on trans people's status, equality and protection.

sources.title: Poland: School Censorship Proposal Threatens Basic Rights | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch (Mar 2007): 'Poland: School Censorship Proposal Threatens Basic Rights' — warns the proposed penal-code amendment would criminalise virtually all school discussion of homosexuality, targeting LGBT education and anti-discrimination work.
